summary: Make a dark rig say so, without changing a transmitted byte, a wire schema, or a rendered pixel. The skeleton is opus's — the highest-scoring variant under both attacks (parity 5/5, and its two structural claims were verified against source by the fable reviewer rather than merely asserted): reuse `OutputStatus.lastError`, which is already on the wire (packages/protocol/src/index.ts:110) and already renders as a pulsing red ERR pill AHEAD of the LIVE branch (apps/web/src/lib/app/chrome/output-pill.ts:64), so the whole fix lands with zero protocol, zod, or UI change; and subscribe from OutputManager rather than main.ts, which additionally means BOTH render hosts are covered by one change (engine-host.ts:61 and voice-engine-host.ts:120 each construct their own OutputManager, and main.ts:466-467 already binds the monitor sink to both) — load-bearing given that every shipping path forces the voice engine. Three grafts changed the shape. (1) From fable's subtraction skeleton, the part that survived: the identical ~25-line status block opus was willing to duplicate across both adapters is extracted — but ONLY the pure part, a package-private `StatusLatch` with an injectable clock. The socket-lifecycle collapse fable actually proposed is dropped, because both reviewers landed on it (setBroadcast/reuseAddr/setMulticastInterface/setMulticastTTL are unobservable on loopback and are exactly what the collapse must reproduce in a zero-coverage region). Extracting only the pure half kills three separate attacks at once: it gives the rate limiter a fake-clock home so opus's undeterminable S9(b) becomes one assertion, it forces latch equality to be defined as (state, code) rather than a message string, and it makes the unconditional error floor a single tested rule instead of a per-adapter comment. (2) From sonnet: the full enumeration of all four `implements PixelOutput` fakes, and its sharper known_gaps language about a post-bind interface deprecation that dgram may never report at all. Sonnet's fail-closed arming and its per-send `checkUniverse` guard are DROPPED — both reviewers broke them (a silent early return in the transmit path is the very pattern this initiative exists to delete, and refusing to arm every default 0-based sACN project is a product regression sonnet's own open question marked blocks_execution:true). (3) Consequently the universe half ships warn-only, one notch quieter even than opus: no `lastError`, no red pill, no error-typed monitor row, emitted AFTER the existing settings row so the pre-existing 'keeps output monitor destination and source fields filterable' test keeps passing unchanged. Whether it should be louder is Trent's call, and nothing in this plan blocks on it. Transport faults also get their own `transportError` slot composed into `status().lastError` rather than overwriting the shared one — the repair both reviewers demanded of both rivals — so an asynchronous transport status can neither clear nor hide a synchronous send/blackout failure.

design.title: Characterization net: hermetic socket-lifecycle tests that pin today's silent failure
design.intent: packages/io has zero coverage of the UDP socket lifecycle — artnet.test.ts and sacn.test.ts exercise only encodeArtDmx / encodeE131 / sacnMulticastAddress. Nothing may be changed in a 0%-coverage region until a net exists under it. This step adds no production code: it records, as executable assertions, what ArtNetOutput and SacnOutput do today INCLUDING the bug, so every later change is measured against recorded fact rather than intuition. Later steps invert those assertions and the test diff becomes the behaviour-change record.
design.verification: New packages/io/src/artnet.socket.test.ts: (a) 'happy path delivers a packet' — bind a dgram.createSocket('udp4') receiver on 127.0.0.1 port 0, read address().port, construct new ArtNetOutput({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: boundPort, iface: '127.0.0.1' }), nextFrame(), send(1, new Uint8Array(512)), and await a message-event promise (event-driven, no sleep; vitest timeout 2000ms) asserting the received buffer starts with `Art-Net\0`, is 530 bytes, and is byte-equal to encodeArtDmx(1, seq, data) — this recorded buffer is the golden fixture S5 compares against. (b) 'a bind failure is currently silent' — construct new ArtNetOutput({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: boundPort, iface: '203.0.113.9' }) (TEST-NET-3, RFC 5737, never assigned to a NIC), assert send() does not throw, and assert the object exposes no status channel: expect('onStatus' in out).toBe(false) — the assertion S4/S5 deliberately invert. The 'receiver got nothing' half is stated in the test name and a comment as an EXPLICITLY TIMING-BOUNDED negative assertion with a generous 1000ms budget, never as a deterministic proof (repairing the attack that a 300ms wait in a file claiming 'no fixed sleeps' is both a flake source and a proof-by-timeout). Mirror both in sacn.socket.test.ts against 127.0.0.1 with an explicit `host` (unicast — CI has no multicast fabric), recording the 638-byte E1.31 golden fixture. Close every socket in afterEach. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: Delete the two new test files; no production code was touched.

design.title: De-duplicate ipToInt/intToIp into packages/io/src/net/ipv4.ts
design.intent: duplicated-code-0012. Four private declarations of two byte-identical functions (apps/server/src/network-adapters.ts:32-46 and packages/io/src/pixlite/sweep.ts:28-42) collapse to two exported ones in the lower package; apps/server already declares @ledrums/io (apps/server/package.json:17). The destination is a new net/ipv4.ts, NOT an export lifted out of sweep.ts: packages/io/src/pixlite/index.ts is a curated named barrel whose header scopes it to 'PixLite Mk3 controller client', so exporting generic IPv4 codecs through it would read as accidental to the next caller — the attack that broke the rival placement. Mechanical and behaviour-preserving by construction: the `invalid IPv4 address: ${addr}` throw and per-octet range check move verbatim, so listNetworkAdapters's skip-a-bad-NIC try/catch and expandCidr's throw keep firing identically.
design.verification: New packages/io/src/net/ipv4.ts exports `ipToInt(addr: string): number` and `intToIp(n: number): string`, copied character-for-character from packages/io/src/pixlite/sweep.ts:28-42 (error message text and the `(n * 256 + o) >>> 0` accumulation included). Add `export * from './net/ipv4';` to packages/io/src/index.ts. Delete both private copies; sweep.ts imports from '../net/ipv4', network-adapters.ts imports { ipToInt, intToIp } from '@ledrums/io'. New packages/io/src/net/ipv4.test.ts pins the failure path the copies carried: expect(() => ipToInt('1.2.3')).toThrow('invalid IPv4 address: 1.2.3'); ipToInt('1.2.3.256') throws; ipToInt('a.b.c.d') throws; ipToInt('255.255.255.255') === 4294967295; intToIp(ipToInt('192.168.1.50')) === '192.168.1.50'. PARITY PROOF: apps/server/src/network-adapters.test.ts and packages/io/src/pixlite/sweep.test.ts must pass with ZERO edits. Run: `pnpm gates`, then `grep -rn 'function ipToInt' apps packages` and `grep -rn 'function intToIp' apps packages` must each return exactly one hit.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit; the private copies return and no later step depends on this file.

design.title: Package-private StatusLatch: the pure, fake-clock-testable half of the status seam
design.intent: The one graft from the subtraction variant that survived both attacks. Both adapters would otherwise carry an identical ~25-line block of handler list + latch + replay + rate limit, and the rival plan's version of that limiter was broken three ways: an alternating error/ready flap resets the latch so a per-code floor never engages; 'emit only when it differs from the latch' never defines the equality key, so variable dgram message text defeats it; and a floor built on a bare Date.now() inside an adapter has no injectable clock, making any 'at most N per second' assertion undeterminable. Extracting ONLY the pure part — no socket, no dgram, no IO — fixes all three in one tested place. Deliberately NOT exported from packages/io/src/index.ts: it is an implementation detail with exactly two internal callers, so the public surface does not grow. The socket lifecycle itself (createSocket/bind/setBroadcast/reuseAddr/setMulticastInterface/setMulticastTTL/close) is deliberately NOT collapsed here — see open_questions.
design.verification: New packages/io/src/status-latch.ts exports (from the file only) `class StatusLatch<T extends { state: string; code?: string }>` with `constructor(opts?: { now?: () => number; minIntervalMs?: number })` (defaults `Date.now`, 1000). API: `get latched(): T | null`; `subscribe(h: (s: T) => void): void` — pushes and, when a status is latched, replays it to that handler immediately, INSIDE try/catch; `set(status: T): void` — computes `key = ${status.state}|${status.code ?? ''}`, always updates `latched`, and emits to every handler (each inside its own try/catch) only when key !== lastEmittedKey AND now() - lastEmitMs >= minIntervalMs, then records lastEmittedKey/lastEmitMs. lastEmitMs starts at -Infinity so the FIRST status of any kind emits immediately — a bind failure is never delayed. Tests in status-latch.test.ts with an injected fake clock, each a single deterministic assertion: (a) first set emits immediately; (b) 1000 sets of the same (state, code) with different `error` strings emit exactly once — equality is (state, code), never the message; (c) 1000 sets ALTERNATING error/ready at 44Hz fake time over one fake second emit at most 2 times (this is the flap attack that broke the rival limiter; assert an exact number, not a bound expressed in prose); (d) a subscriber attaching after a latch is replayed the latched value exactly once; (e) a handler that throws does not propagate out of set() or subscribe(), and the remaining handlers still run; (f) a state change suppressed by the floor is emitted by the next set() once the interval has elapsed. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: `git revert`; the file has no importer until S5/S6.

design.title: Add PixelOutputStatus to packages/io/src/interfaces.ts as an OPTIONAL method (type-only, inert)
design.intent: Give PixelOutput the observability channel it has never had, mirroring OscInputStatus (packages/io/src/osc.ts:205-216) so the house pattern from d1d6eb9 is applied rather than reinvented. `onStatus` is declared OPTIONAL, and that is the whole risk-first point: FOUR test doubles declare `class FakeOutput implements PixelOutput` — apps/server/src/output-manager.test.ts:16, apps/server/src/engine-host.test.ts:7, apps/server/src/voice-engine-host.test.ts:7 and apps/server/src/handlers/voice-input.test.ts:15 — and a REQUIRED member would land this wave typecheck-red against all four, the attack that broke both rival variants. Optional means zero edits outside this one file and zero runtime bytes changed.
design.verification: Add `export interface PixelOutputStatus { state: 'ready' | 'error'; error?: string; code?: string }` and `onStatus?(handler: (s: PixelOutputStatus) => void): void;` to PixelOutput, with a doc comment stating the latch-and-replay contract in the spirit of osc.ts:275-280. INERTNESS PROOF, all three required: `git show --stat` for this commit lists exactly one file; `pnpm typecheck` passes with no edit to artnet.ts, sacn.ts, output-manager.ts or any of the four fake files named above; and `grep -rn 'implements PixelOutput' apps packages` still returns exactly those six sites (four fakes + ArtNetOutput + SacnOutput) with none of them modified. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: `git revert`; nothing implements or calls onStatus until S5/S6.

design.title: ArtNetOutput adopts StatusLatch — the total swallow is replaced, transmit path untouched
design.intent: Turn `this.socket.on('error', () => {})` (artnet.ts:49) and the send-completion `() => {}` (artnet.ts:74) into status emissions through the S3 latch. The transmit semantics do not change: send() keeps its `if (!this.ready) return;` early return gated on the SAME bind-set boolean, the encoder is untouched, and every emit happens inside dgram's asynchronous callbacks — off the render loop's stack — so the fire-and-forget non-negotiable holds. Critically, the transmit gate is NEVER coupled to the status latch: a send-completion error latches an observable status but does not stop later sends, so a transient EHOSTUNREACH cannot darken a rig that baseline would have kept transmitting through. That coupling is what broke a rival variant. The setBroadcast try/catch at artnet.ts:51-57 also stops being silent: it emits an error status and still proceeds to ready, preserving today's transmit behaviour exactly.
design.verification: In ArtNetOutput replace nothing on the send path; add `private readonly status = new StatusLatch<PixelOutputStatus>(opts.now ? { now: opts.now } : {})` (ArtNetOptions gains an optional `now?: () => number` used by tests only), `onStatus(h) { this.status.subscribe(h); }`, and wire three call sites: `this.socket.on('error', (err: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => this.status.set({ state: 'error', error: err.message, ...(err.code ? { code: err.code } : {}) }))`; onBound sets `this.ready = true` and then `this.status.set({ state: 'ready' })`; the setBroadcast catch sets `{ state: 'error', error: `broadcast unavailable: ${String(err)}`, code: 'EBROADCAST' }` and still falls through to ready; `this.socket.send(pkt, this.port, this.host, (err) => { if (err) this.status.set({ state: 'error', error: err.message, ...((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ? { code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code } : {}) }); })`. Tests in artnet.socket.test.ts: (a) INVERT S1(b) — iface '203.0.113.9' now yields an onStatus error within 2000ms with state 'error', a non-empty `error`, and code EADDRNOTAVAIL or EINVAL (platform-dependent, both accepted); (b) WIRE PARITY — the happy path emits { state: 'ready' } and the loopback receiver's 530-byte buffer is byte-compared against the golden fixture recorded in S1(a) before the adapter was touched; (c) a subscriber attaching after the bind resolves is replayed the latched status; (d) a subscriber that throws does not throw out of send() and does not reach the process — install a `process.once('uncaughtException', …)` / `process.once('unhandledRejection', …)` sentinel for the test's duration and assert it never fires (a listeners-COUNT assertion proves nothing, since an uncaught exception does not change the count — the repair for the attack that landed on the rival's version of this test); (e) a broadcast-mode instance still calls socket.setBroadcast(true) — spy on the socket and assert the call, so the option cannot be silently dropped. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit restores the `() => {}` swallow. Safe at any time because nothing subscribes until S7; with S7 landed, reverting S5 leaves `onStatus` undefined on ArtNetOutput and S7's optional-chained `this.output.onStatus?.(...)` becomes a no-op — exactly pre-change behaviour. Independent of S6 (different file, different class).

design.title: SacnOutput adopts StatusLatch, including the swallowed multicast-interface failure
design.intent: Same seam, same latch, plus the sACN-specific hole the finding never enumerated and only one variant caught — the hole that matters MOST for the headline scenario. SacnOutput's bind takes no address (sacn.ts:96), so a stale `iface` NEVER produces a bind error on sACN; it fails inside the bare `catch { /* ignore */ }` around setMulticastInterface(opts.iface)/setMulticastTTL(16) at sacn.ts:97-102, after which multicast silently leaves the DEFAULT NIC instead of the operator's chosen one. Any plan that only fixes bind and send-completion errors misses the ethernet-to-wifi dark-rig path on sACN entirely — and a test asserting a bind-time EADDRNOTAVAIL for a bad sACN iface can only ever hang to timeout. Emitting from that catch while STILL setting ready preserves transmit behaviour exactly and adds only the diagnosis.
design.verification: Add the same `StatusLatch` member, `onStatus`, and optional `now` test hook to SacnOutput (no duplicated limiter logic — that is what S3 bought). Wire: `this.socket.on('error', …)` emits instead of swallowing; the bind callback emits { state: 'ready' } after `this.ready = true`; the inner catch around setMulticastInterface/setMulticastTTL emits `{ state: 'error', error: `multicast interface ${opts.iface} unavailable: ${String(err)}`, code: 'EMCASTIFACE' }` and then still falls through to ready; the send completion callback emits on err. Tests in sacn.socket.test.ts: (a) WIRE PARITY — the loopback unicast receiver's 638-byte E1.31 buffer is byte-compared against the S1 golden fixture, plus a { state: 'ready' } status; (b) `new SacnOutput({ iface: '203.0.113.9', host: '127.0.0.1', port: boundPort })` emits state 'error' with code EMCASTIFACE AND send() still delivers to the receiver — the single test that proves observability was added while transmit behaviour was not changed; (c) late-subscriber replay; (d) throwing-subscriber sentinel as in S5(d); (e) the socket is still created with `{ type: 'udp4', reuseAddr: true }` and setMulticastTTL(16) is still called — spy assertions, so neither option can be silently dropped. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit restores both swallows. Independent of S5 (different file, different class), and inert until S7 for the same optional-method reason.

design.title: OutputManager subscribes; transport faults get their own slot, composed into the existing lastError
design.intent: The step that turns the seam on, and the reason no protocol, schema or UI change is needed anywhere: OutputStatus.lastError (packages/protocol/src/index.ts:110) already reaches every client on `state` and on every `stats` tick, and apps/web/src/lib/app/chrome/output-pill.ts:64 branches on it BEFORE the LIVE branch, so a transport fault immediately reads as a pulsing red ERR with the message in the tooltip. Subscribing here rather than in main.ts also covers BOTH render hosts with one change — engine-host.ts:61 and voice-engine-host.ts:120 each construct an OutputManager and main.ts:466-467 already binds the monitor sink to both — which matters because every shipping path forces the voice engine. Transport faults are stored in a NEW private `transportError` field, never in the shared `lastError` slot: both reviewers landed the same attack on both rival variants, that an asynchronous transport status writing or clearing the shared slot silently destroys a fault written by the synchronous send (output-manager.ts:226) or blackout (output-manager.ts:256) paths. Composing instead of overwriting means neither can hide the other, and no wire field is added.
design.verification: Add `private transportError: string | null = null;` and `private transportGen = 0;`. In applySettings, immediately after `this.output = this.factory(settings)` succeeds (output-manager.ts:108) and beside the existing `this.lastError = null` at :110, also set `this.transportError = null`, take `const gen = ++this.transportGen;`, and call `this.output.onStatus?.((s) => { if (gen !== this.transportGen) return; if (s.state !== 'error') return; this.transportError = s.code ? `${s.code}: ${s.error ?? 'transport error'}` : (s.error ?? 'transport error'); this.monitorError('Output transport error', settings, this.transportError); });`. The generation guard is parity-critical: teardown() (output-manager.ts:125-132) drops this.output but a closed dgram socket can still fire queued callbacks, and without it a dead transport would write fault state for a transport that no longer exists. status() changes ONE line: `lastError: [this.lastError, this.transportError].filter(Boolean).join(' | ') || null` — still one nullable string on the wire, outputStatusSchema untouched. A 'ready' status deliberately clears NOTHING; transportError resets only on transport (re)construction, matching the existing contract at :110 exactly. Do NOT touch sendFrame, blackout, the state machine, or any public method signature. New tests extending the existing local FakeOutput with an onStatus/emit pair: (a) 'a transport error reaches lastError' — arm, emit { state: 'error', error: 'bind failed', code: 'EADDRNOTAVAIL' }, assert status().lastError contains 'EADDRNOTAVAIL'; (b) 'a transport error reaches the monitor bus' — assert exactly one event with type 'error' and source 'server/output'; (c) 'a ready status clears nothing' — latch a transport error, emit { state: 'ready' }, assert status().lastError still contains it; (d) 'a transport ready cannot erase a synchronous send failure' — drive the existing throwing-FakeOutput send path to set lastError, then emit { state: 'ready' } and then { state: 'error' }, and assert BOTH messages are present in status().lastError, joined; (e) 'a status from a torn-down transport is ignored' — arm, capture the fake, applySettings(disabled), emit an error from the captured fake, assert status().lastError unchanged; (f) 'a PixelOutput with no onStatus still arms and transmits' — the optional-method compatibility proof using a bare fake with only nextFrame/send/close. Every one of the ~30 existing tests in apps/server/src/output-manager.test.ts must pass UNCHANGED. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: `git revert` of this ONE commit restores byte-exact pre-initiative server behaviour: the io status seam stays landed but has no subscriber, so both adapters emit into an empty handler list and status().lastError reverts to send/blackout throws only. This is the designated rollback boundary for the whole initiative. If S9 has already landed, revert S9 first — it touches the same file.

design.title: Pure protocol-universe domain predicate in packages/io/src/universe.ts
design.intent: primitive-obsession-0006. Give the universe invariant a single named home without branding a type across packages/core and without renumbering anything. packages/io declares no dependency on @ledrums/core (packages/io/package.json has no such dep), so the protocol union is declared locally and structurally matches Project['output']['protocol']. Pure — no IO, no sockets, no caller yet — a step that cannot break anything.
design.verification: New packages/io/src/universe.ts exports `type OutputProtocolTag = 'artnet' | 'sacn'`, `SACN_UNIVERSE_MIN = 1`, `SACN_UNIVERSE_MAX = 63999`, `universeDomain(protocol): { min: number; max: number }` (artnet → { min: 0, max: 32767 } per the 15-bit field at artnet.ts:22-23; sacn → { min: 1, max: 63999 } per ANSI E1.31), and `isUniverseValid(protocol, universe): boolean` (integer check plus range). A doc comment records WHY: sacnMulticastAddress(0) yields '239.255.0.0', which is not a valid E1.31 universe group. Add `export * from './universe';` to packages/io/src/index.ts. New packages/io/src/universe.test.ts: isUniverseValid('sacn', 0) false; ('sacn', 1) true; ('sacn', 63999) true; ('sacn', 64000) false; ('sacn', 1.5) false; ('artnet', 0) true; ('artnet', 32767) true; ('artnet', 32768) false; plus a cross-check asserting sacnMulticastAddress(0) === '239.255.0.0' and sacnMulticastAddress(SACN_UNIVERSE_MIN) === '239.255.0.1', documenting the exact defect. Run: `pnpm gates`. No production file outside packages/io/src/index.ts changes.
design.reverses: `git revert`; no caller exists until S9.

design.title: Warn-only sACN universe-domain audit at the arm seam — detect, never renumber, never redden
design.intent: Make the dead-multicast-group condition visible at arm time, at the one place that knows both the protocol and the DmxMap, without touching packages/core, buildDmxMap, or a single transmitted byte. Two rival designs were broken here and both breakages shaped this step. Refusing to arm was rejected: it turns 'transmits to a dead group' into 'will not arm at all' for every project whose map is the default 0-based one (dmx-map.ts:99-102 seeds the cursor at 0), a live-show regression whose own plan marked the decision blocks_execution:true. A per-send `checkUniverse` early return in the adapters was also rejected: it is a silent drop in the render-loop transmit path — the exact pattern this initiative exists to delete — and it would stop sACN UNICAST universe-0 frames that reach a real receiver today (sacn.ts:114 uses opts.host when set, bypassing the multicast address) while OutputManager kept incrementing packetsSent. This step therefore ships one notch quieter even than the skeleton it came from: an informational monitor row only, never `type: 'error'`, never touching lastError or transportError, so no operator gets a surprise red pill on upgrade. How loud it should be is Trent's, and nothing blocks on it.
design.verification: In applySettings, AFTER the existing `this.monitorSettings(settings, dmxMap)` call at :122 (ordering is load-bearing — the pre-existing test 'keeps output monitor destination and source fields filterable' asserts events[0] is the settings row, and that test arms sacn against a single-universe-0 fixture, so an audit row emitted earlier would break it), compute `const bad = dmxMap.universes.filter((u) => !isUniverseValid(settings.protocol === 'sacn' ? 'sacn' : 'artnet', u.universe)).map((u) => u.universe);`. Dedup with its OWN key field `universeAuditSignature = `${settings.protocol}|${settings.state}|${bad.join(',')}``, NOT by extending settingsMonitorSignature and NOT by bad.length: that signature (output-manager.ts:285) carries only universes.LENGTH, so editing startUniverse from 1 to 0 turns [1,2] into [0,1] — same length, same settings, signature unchanged — and the diagnostic would miss precisely the valid→invalid transition it exists for. Both reviewers landed this attack, against two different variants. When bad.length > 0 emit exactly one `this.onMonitor?.({ type: 'output', direction: 'out', source: 'server/output', destination: outputDestination(settings), label: 'Universes outside protocol range', detail: `sacn universes ${bad.join(',')} are outside E1.31 1..63999 — universe 0 multicasts to 239.255.0.0, a dead group; set startUniverse on the output` })`. sendFrame and blackout are NOT touched. New tests: (a) 'sACN with a 0-based map emits one informational row' — protocol sacn, map containing universe 0 → exactly one type 'output' event naming the universes, and status().lastError === null; (b) 'the audit does not fire twice for an unchanged map' — two applySettings calls with the same map emit one row; (c) 'an equal-count change of WHICH universes are bad re-fires' — apply [1,2] then [0,1]; assert a second row (the dedup-key regression lock); (d) 'Art-Net universe 0 is silent' — universe 0 is legal Art-Net, assert no audit event at all; (e) 'the audit changes no transmitted bytes' — capture the FakeOutput sends for the sACN universe-0 fixture and byte-compare against the pre-S9 capture from the existing 'armed transmits one packet per universe' fixture; (f) the pre-existing 'keeps output monitor destination and source fields filterable' test passes UNCHANGED, proving the ordering. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit; it removes only diagnostics and is independent of S7 (different code path in the same file — if reverting S7 too, revert S9 first).

design.title: Non-negotiable regression locks: no work in the send path, no flood, no crash-by-subscriber
design.intent: The three ways this initiative could violate AGENTS.md's non-negotiables each get a named, failing-if-broken test, so a later refactor cannot quietly reintroduce them. Each asserts a property the plan claims and that nothing else in the suite would catch. The rate-limit lock lives in S3's pure fake-clock tests, not here, so this step contains no undeterminable timing assertion and no implementer-choice branch.
design.verification: (a) 'sendFrame performs no work proportional to status subscribers' — register 100 status handlers on the FakeOutput, run 100 sendFrame calls, assert zero handler invocations (status is emitted only from socket callbacks, never from the send path). (b) 'the manager forwards transport errors 1:1 and the adapter latch is what bounds them' — emit 1000 error statuses through the FakeOutput and assert 1000 monitor rows, with a comment pointing at status-latch.test.ts case (c) as the place the 44Hz flap bound is actually proven; this is a single unambiguous assertion, replacing the two mutually exclusive branches the reviewer broke. (c) 'a throwing monitor sink cannot kill an armed transport' — set onMonitor to a thrower, emit a transport error, assert sendFrame still runs and does not throw. (d) STRUCTURAL no-sync-IO lock in artnet.socket.test.ts, replacing the wall-clock bound a reviewer showed can both false-fail under the gates mutex and false-pass at 1ms/send: stub the socket's send with a recorder and assert ArtNetOutput.send() RETURNS BEFORE the completion callback runs (proving nothing awaits it), plus a source-level assertion that readFileSync of artnet.ts and sacn.ts contains no `await`, `execSync`, or `Atomics.wait`. Keep a wall-clock smoke check of 44 successive real-socket sends with a deliberately generous 250ms budget, labelled in the test name as a smoke check, not a proof. Run: `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: Delete the added test cases; no production code in this step.

design.title: docs-truth pass on every comment that asserts the old silent-failure contract
design.intent: Three prominent doc comments describe the world this initiative just changed. Leaving them is a documentation lie that will lead the next reader to re-derive the same finding. Comment-only, zero behaviour, zero rendered output.
design.verification: (1) packages/io/src/interfaces.ts — the PixelOutput header keeps 'Fire-and-forget' (still true) and gains a sentence that transport liveness is now observable via onStatus, mirroring OscInput. (2) apps/server/src/output-manager.ts — the class doc at :70-74 says 'any transition away from armed, or a send error, emits a blackout failsafe'; add that an ASYNCHRONOUS transport fault latches transportError and emits a monitor error but does NOT blackout (there is nothing to blacken — the socket is already not transmitting), and that status().lastError composes the synchronous and transport slots. (3) apps/web/src/lib/app/chrome/output-pill.ts — its header says 'a socket can be open and green while output is actually failing'; extend it to state that lastError now also carries bind-time, multicast-interface and send-completion transport faults from packages/io, so ERR fires on a stale-iface failure that previously showed LIVE. AGENTS.md UI GATE DISCHARGED EXPLICITLY: the apps/web edit is comment-only, and the verification is a mechanical proof of that — `git diff -U0 -- apps/web | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -vE '^[+-][+-]'` must show only lines inside the leading block comment, so rendered output is provably unchanged and the /make-interfaces-feel-better + `pnpm ui-shot` rules (which govern changes to rendered UI) have nothing to bite on. If a reviewer disputes that reading, drop file (3) from this step and land the pill comment in a separate UI-gated change — the rest of the step is unaffected. Plus `pnpm gates` green and `grep -rn "() => {}" packages/io/src/artnet.ts packages/io/src/sacn.ts` returns no error-swallowing callback.

interface_deltas.note: Deliberate. A resilience initiative buys observability with interface, and the objective function cannot be satisfied by a plan that removes the ability to see a dark rig. Three mitigations, each verifiable: (1) ipToInt/intToIp are a net REDUCTION in declarations — four private copies become two shared exports, which is the whole of duplicated-code-0012; (2) onStatus is OPTIONAL, so none of the four existing FakeOutput implementors is forced to grow; (3) StatusLatch — the ~25-line block both adapters would otherwise duplicate — is package-private and deliberately NOT re-exported from index.ts, so the shared machinery adds zero public surface. The universe symbols are pure predicates with no runtime cost and no caller in the hot path.

The scoring claim of this plan. The entire server-side fix lands behind surfaces that already exist — OutputStatus.lastError, OutputManager.onMonitor, status() — so OutputManager's public methods are identical in shape before and after, no symbol is added to apps/server, and the new transportError field is private and composed into the existing nullable string. Subscribing here rather than in main.ts additionally covers both EngineHost and VoiceEngineHost with one change, and keeps the 935-line main.ts god-file untouched.

Explicitly untouched. The finding's proposed fix implied new wire fields; reusing lastError avoids a zod schema change, avoids the _LockOutputStatus type-assertion churn in packages/protocol/src/schemas.ts, and avoids any UI work at all. An old web client against a new server and a new client against an old server both keep working, because the wire shape did not change.

checks: pnpm gates — after EVERY step, not only at the end; each of S1..S11 is its own green commit. Baseline is 2968 tests at sha 3708648 plus fix batches 1-3 already landed; the count must only ever rise.
S2 parity: apps/server/src/network-adapters.test.ts and packages/io/src/pixlite/sweep.test.ts pass with ZERO edits — the dedup is proven by untouched consumers, not by a new test.
S2 residue: `grep -rn 'function ipToInt' apps packages` and `grep -rn 'function intToIp' apps packages` each return exactly one hit.

S3 determinism: status-latch.test.ts runs entirely on an injected fake clock — 1000 alternating error/ready sets across one fake second emit at most 2 times, asserted as an exact number. This is the only rate-limit assertion in the plan; no wall-clock timing anywhere is presented as proof.

S4 inertness: `git show --stat` for the S4 commit lists exactly packages/io/src/interfaces.ts, `pnpm typecheck` passes, and all four `implements PixelOutput` fakes (apps/server/src/output-manager.test.ts:16, engine-host.test.ts:7, voice-engine-host.test.ts:7, handlers/voice-input.test.ts:15) are unmodified.

S5/S6 wire parity: the loopback receive-socket assertions byte-compare the 530-byte Art-Net packet and the 638-byte E1.31 packet against the exact golden fixtures recorded in S1 BEFORE either adapter was touched.

S5/S6 socket-option locks: spy assertions that setBroadcast(true) still fires in broadcast mode, and that SacnOutput is still constructed with reuseAddr:true and still calls setMulticastTTL(16) — so no option can be silently dropped while every other check stays green.

S5/S6 failure-path proof: ArtNetOutput with iface '203.0.113.9' emits an onStatus error within 2000ms (the assertion S1 recorded as impossible), and SacnOutput with a bad iface emits EMCASTIFACE while STILL delivering to a loopback receiver — observability added, transmit behaviour unchanged.

S7 non-regression: all ~30 existing apps/server/src/output-manager.test.ts tests pass unchanged, including 'armed transmits one packet per universe', 'blacks out the rig when transitioning armed -> disabled', and 'records a send error without crashing'.
S7 slot isolation: a transport 'ready' clears nothing, and a synchronous send failure plus a transport error both appear in the composed status().lastError — neither channel can erase the other.

S9 ordering + byte parity: the pre-existing 'keeps output monitor destination and source fields filterable' test passes UNCHANGED (proving the audit row is emitted after the settings row), and the FakeOutput send capture for the sACN universe-0 fixture is byte-compared against the pre-S9 capture.
S9 dedup regression lock: applying [1,2] then [0,1] — equal counts, different bad sets — emits a second audit row.
S10 structural no-sync-IO lock: send() returns before the dgram completion callback runs, and artnet.ts/sacn.ts contain no await/execSync/Atomics.wait.
S11 UI-gate discharge: `git diff -U0 -- apps/web` for the S11 commit shows only comment lines.

Manual hardware gate (not automatable, see known_gaps): arm sACN against the PixLite with `tcpdump -i <nic> udp port 5568` running; confirm pixels light and the packet stream shape is unchanged while the link is healthy; then switch the machine off the configured interface and observe an 'Output transport error' Monitor row and a red ERR pill. Record the result on the initiative's Notion row.
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps: The largest gap is why S1 exists: at baseline the UDP socket lifecycle in packages/io/src/artnet.ts and packages/io/src/sacn.ts has ZERO test coverage — artnet.test.ts and sacn.test.ts exercise only the pure encoders. A green 2968-test suite at HEAD therefore proves nothing whatsoever about bind, ready-gating, multicast setup or send completion, and 'the suite still passes' would be a meaningless parity claim for S5/S6. What replaces it: S1's hermetic characterization tests landed BEFORE any adapter edit, pinning today's behaviour including the bug and recording golden packet fixtures; RFC 5737 TEST-NET-3 (203.0.113.9), guaranteed never assigned to a NIC, which makes the bind-failure path a deterministic network-free unit test; and explicit spy locks on setBroadcast / reuseAddr / setMulticastTTL, because loopback unicast cannot observe any of them and a refactor that dropped one would otherwise leave every stated check green — the attack that broke the lifecycle-collapse variant, and the reason this plan does NOT collapse the socket lifecycle. Four things remain genuinely unprovable in CI. (1) Real multicast egress on the correct NIC after setMulticastInterface: CI has no second NIC and no multicast fabric, so the sACN iface tests use unicast to 127.0.0.1 and prove only that the diagnostic fires, not that packets reached the right wire. (2) The literal ethernet-to-wifi hot-swap: Node's dgram gives no hook for a NIC disappearing under an already-bound socket, and on some OS/driver combinations a post-bind interface deprecation surfaces as NO event at all — the socket may simply start black-holing outbound packets with neither an 'error' event nor a send-callback error. This plan closes every failure the dgram API DOES report (bind error, socket error, multicast-interface setup failure, send-completion error) and is explicit that a fully silent post-bind black-hole is NOT closed; an active liveness probe would be needed and is escalated rather than smuggled in. (3) Whether the operator NOTICES the red pill mid-show — a human-factors question no test answers. (4) The universe work (S8/S9) is verified against the DmxMap shape and the E1.31 spec, not against a controller: whether a PixLite ignores a universe-0 sACN stream in practice is inferred from the spec and from the existing 0→1 conversion at apps/web/src/lib/app/docks/inspectors/PatchOutputInspector.svelte:59-62, not from a packet capture — which is exactly why this plan only reports and never renumbers. One design-level residue is stated rather than tested: StatusLatch suppresses a state change that arrives inside the 1000ms floor and emits it on the next set(); if a flap's final state arrives and NO further status is ever set, that final state stays unemitted. In practice sends run at 44Hz while armed and a transport that stops emitting has been torn down, so the window is bounded by one frame — but it is a real edge, not a proof.
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.baseline_reference: sha 3708648, 2968 tests green under `pnpm gates`, plus fix batches 1-3 already landed (12 dead-code auto-fixes, dead-code residue, kit-mirror removal with the mirror FIELD gone at every layer and setKitGlobal surviving). None of those batches touched packages/io, apps/server/src/output-manager.ts, apps/server/src/network-adapters.ts or packages/io/src/pixlite/sweep.ts, so there is no interaction to reconcile.

rollback_strategy: Eleven separate commits on one branch, each independently revertible, with S7 as the designated single-commit rollback boundary. The ordering is built for this: S3, S4, S5, S6 and S8 are INERT — onStatus is an optional method with no subscriber, StatusLatch has no importer until S5/S6, isUniverseValid has no caller — so nothing observable changes until S7 turns the subscription on and S9 adds the audit row. Backing out has three tiers. (1) Show-day panic: `git revert` the S7 commit alone. The io status seam stays landed but emits into an empty handler list, and server behaviour returns byte-exact to pre-initiative — status().lastError again reflects only synchronous send/blackout throws. If S9 has landed, revert S9 first (same file). (2) Diagnostic too noisy: revert S9 alone to drop the universe audit while keeping transport-error surfacing. (3) Full withdrawal: revert S11, S10, S9, S7, S6, S5, S4, S3, S8, S2, S1 in reverse order; S2 is the only step with a consumer outside packages/io (apps/server/src/network-adapters.ts) and its revert restores the private copies. Nothing here persists state, migrates data, or changes a wire format: packages/protocol is untouched, outputStatusSchema is unchanged, and no zod schema, project file or kit file gains or loses a field — so there is no forward-incompatible artifact to unwind and no version skew in either direction between an old client and a new server. The one irreversible-in-spirit change is operator expectation: once a drummer has seen the ERR pill fire on a dead socket, reverting means going back to a silent rig — a product decision, not a technical one.

open_questions.question: Should a transport fault auto-clear when frames start flowing again, or stay latched until the operator re-arms? This plan ships STICKY: transportError is cleared only on transport (re)construction, matching the existing lastError contract at output-manager.ts:110, and a 'ready' status deliberately clears nothing — which is also what stops an asynchronous recovery from erasing a synchronous send failure. The cost is that one transient EHOSTUNREACH pins the pill red for the rest of the show even after the network recovers. Sticky is the honest-but-annoying choice; auto-clearing risks hiding a flapping link. The show-floor call is Trent's.

When a bind or multicast-interface setup fails from a stale iface (the ethernet-to-wifi headline scenario), should the adapter attempt an automatic re-bind — with backoff, possibly falling back to the default interface — or stay strictly observe-only? This plan is observe-only: auto-recovery changes live-path behaviour mid-show and could start transmitting from an interface the operator did not choose, which is a different failure, not a smaller one.

sACN universe numbering: should buildDmxMap become protocol-aware and emit 1-based universes for sACN, or should the 0-based map stand with the operator setting startUniverse per output? Renumbering silently changes the wire for every existing project — including rigs where the operator ALREADY compensated at the controller or with startUniverse, which it would break. This plan therefore only detects and reports (S8/S9). If taken, renumbering deserves its own initiative with a kit-schema migration.

How loud should the sACN universe-domain audit be? This plan ships the quietest defensible form — an informational monitor row only, never type 'error', never touching lastError — because both louder rivals were broken: refusing to arm regresses every default 0-based sACN project from 'transmits to a dead group' to 'will not arm', and setting lastError would turn the pill red on upgrade for any single-universe-0 sACN config. If Trent wants any dark universe to read as an error, S9 becomes one loud branch and the upgrade is visibly noisier; if he wants arming refused outright, that is a separate gated step, not an edit to S9. Nothing in this plan blocks on the answer.

After this initiative, ArtNetOutput and SacnOutput still each carry their own createSocket/bind/close-try-catch lifecycle (~20 lines of near-identical structure), with only the pure status machinery shared via StatusLatch. Collapsing the rest into a package-private BoundUdpSocket was the rival skeleton and was deliberately NOT taken here, because reviewers showed the socket options that differ between them (setBroadcast vs reuseAddr + setMulticastInterface + setMulticastTTL) are precisely what loopback tests cannot observe, making a collapse in a zero-coverage region unverifiable by CI. Once S1/S5/S6 have landed real socket coverage AND the manual rig gate has been run once, that collapse becomes a provable refactor. Worth a follow-on initiative?

Is an active output-liveness probe worth a follow-on initiative? The plan's known_gaps state that a post-bind interface deprecation may surface as no dgram event at all on some OS/driver combinations — the socket simply black-holes. Closing that needs a periodic self-check or a NIC-change watch, which introduces a timer into a currently timer-free IO adapter and would have to be proven not to touch the render loop. Out of scope here by design.

Should the S7 subscription also push a fresh stateMessage to connected clients on a transport fault (as main.ts:705 does for OSC), or is the next periodic stats broadcast soon enough for the ERR pill? OutputStatus already rides every stats tick, so the worst case is one tick of latency; decidable from how often stateMessage already flows without escalating.

synthesis_inputs.rationale: SKELETON: opus, on both reviewers' numbers (parity_preservation 5/5, and its two structural claims — that OutputStatus.lastError is already on the wire and that output-pill.ts:64 branches on it ahead of LIVE — were independently verified against the worktree by the fable reviewer rather than merely asserted). Kept from it: the zero-protocol/zero-UI reuse of lastError; the optional onStatus that leaves all four FakeOutput doubles untouched (the requirement that broke both rivals); the S1-before-anything characterization net for a 0%-coverage region; the generation guard against a torn-down transport (survived both reviewers); routing the subscription through OutputManager rather than the 935-line main.ts — reinforced here by a fact none of the three variants named, that engine-host.ts:61 and voice-engine-host.ts:120 each construct their own OutputManager, so one subscription covers both hosts on a shipping path that always forces the voice engine; and the sACN setMulticastInterface catch, which only opus caught and which is the ONLY path by which a stale iface darkens sACN at all (sacn.ts:96 binds with no address). GRAFTED FROM FABLE: its subtraction instinct, narrowed to the half that survives. Both reviewers broke the BoundUdpSocket lifecycle collapse (setBroadcast/reuseAddr/setMulticastInterface/setMulticastTTL are invisible to loopback tests, so no listed verification would fail if one were dropped; blast_radius_honesty and sequencing_realism scored 2 there), so the collapse is dropped and replaced by spy locks on those exact options in S5/S6. What IS grafted is a package-private StatusLatch (S3) holding only the pure handler/latch/floor logic — which simultaneously repairs three landed attacks: opus's rate limiter being bypassed by an error→ready→error flap (the floor is now unconditional and time-based, tested with 1000 alternating sets), fable's undefined latch equality (fixed as (state, code), never the message string), and opus's S9(b) undeterminable assertion (the clock is injectable and the test is one exact number, so the two-branch 'state which holds in the commit message' verification is deleted). This also resolves opus's own synthesis-owned open question about whether to extract a shared status emitter: yes for the pure part, no for the socket lifecycle. GRAFTED FROM SONNET: the complete enumeration of all four `implements PixelOutput` fakes with file:line (folded into S4's inertness proof), and its sharper known_gaps framing that a post-bind interface deprecation may produce NO dgram event at all — stronger than opus's version, which only said the hot-swap could not be simulated. DROPPED FROM SONNET: fail-closed arming (both reviewers landed it — it regresses every default 0-based sACN project from 'transmits to a dead group' to 'will not arm', and its own open question carried blocks_execution:true), the per-send checkUniverse guard in the adapters (both reviewers landed it — a silent early return in the transmit path is the pattern this initiative exists to delete, and it would stop sACN-unicast universe-0 frames that reach a real receiver today while packetsSent kept incrementing), the ready-clears-lastError convention (both reviewers landed it against both rivals), and the send-gate coupled to the status latch (which would let one transient send error permanently darken a rig that baseline kept transmitting through). REPAIRS FORCED BY SURVIVING ATTACKS, each visible as a changed step: transport faults get their own transportError field composed into status().lastError so neither channel can erase the other (S7 (c) and (d)); the universe audit dedups on bad.join(',') not bad.length or settingsMonitorSignature, with an explicit equal-count regression test (S9 (c)) — an attack both reviewers landed, against two different variants; the throwing-subscriber test uses a real uncaughtException/unhandledRejection sentinel instead of an ineffectual process.listeners count (S5 (d)); the 50ms wall-clock 'no sync IO' lock is replaced by a structural assertion plus a 250ms smoke check (S10 (d)); S1's negative bind assertion is restated as an explicitly timing-bounded claim with a 1000ms budget rather than presented as sleep-free; the ipv4 pair goes to net/ipv4.ts rather than out of the PixLite named barrel (whose header scopes it to the controller client); and S11 discharges the AGENTS.md ui-shot rule mechanically by proving the apps/web edit is comment-only, with a stated fallback of dropping that file. TIGHTER THAN EVERY VARIANT: the universe audit ships informational-only — no lastError, no error-typed row — and is emitted AFTER monitorSettings, because the pre-existing 'keeps output monitor destination and source fields filterable' test arms sACN against a single-universe-0 fixture and asserts events[0]; opus's grading would have made that fixture the all-bad case, reddening the pill and reordering that test's events. That ordering is now a named verification (S9 (f)).
attacks_addressed: opus/S4: the 1000ms error floor is bypassed by an error→ready→error flap because a successful send re-latches 'ready' — repaired by an unconditional time floor inside StatusLatch (S3), proven by an exact-count fake-clock test over 1000 alternating sets.

opus/S9(b): verification offered two mutually exclusive assertions and deferred the choice to the implementer, and the adapter limiter had no injectable clock — repaired by moving the rate-limit assertion into the pure StatusLatch with an injected clock (S3) and reducing S10(b) to a single forwarding assertion.

opus/S3: understated blast radius — only one of four `implements PixelOutput` fakes was named — repaired by naming all four with file:line and making 'none of them modified' part of S4's inertness proof.

opus/S1: a fixed 300ms negative wait in a file claiming 'no fixed sleeps' is both a flake source and a proof-by-timeout — repaired by restating it as an explicitly timing-bounded negative assertion with a 1000ms budget.

opus/S10 (now S11): editing apps/web/src/lib/app/chrome/output-pill.ts triggers AGENTS.md's /make-interfaces-feel-better + `pnpm ui-shot` rules — repaired by a mechanical comment-only proof (`git diff -U0 -- apps/web` shows only comment lines) with an explicit fallback of dropping that file into a separate UI-gated change.

opus/S8 and fable/S4 (the same attack from both reviewers): the diagnostic's dedup key cannot see an equal-count change in WHICH universes are bad ([0,1] → [1,2] via a startUniverse edit), so it misses the exact valid→invalid transition it exists for — repaired by a dedicated universeAuditSignature keyed on bad.join(','), with test (c) as the regression lock.

opus/S4 test (e): asserting 'no uncaughtException' via an unchanged process.listeners count cannot fail for the reason it exists — repaired with a real process.once('uncaughtException'/'unhandledRejection') sentinel for the test's duration.

opus/S9(d): a 44-send/50ms wall-clock bound both false-fails under the gates mutex and false-passes at 1ms/send — repaired by a structural assertion (send() returns before the completion callback; no await/execSync/Atomics.wait in the adapter sources) plus a generous 250ms smoke check labelled as such.

sonnet/S6 (both reviewers): fail-closed arming is a live-show regression governed by a blocks_execution:true question — dropped; the audit ships warn-only and the loudness question is escalated without blocking any step.

sonnet/S6 (both reviewers): the in-adapter `if (!checkUniverse(...)) return;` guard is a silent drop in the render-loop transmit path, allocates per send at 44Hz×N, and breaks sACN-unicast universe-0 delivery while packetsSent keeps incrementing — dropped entirely; enforcement stays at the arm seam and is diagnostic-only.

sonnet/S5 and fable/S3 (both reviewers, both variants): clearing the shared lastError on a transport 'ready' destroys fault state written by the synchronous send/blackout paths — repaired by a dedicated transportError field composed into status().lastError, with tests (c) and (d) in S7.

sonnet/S4: the transmit gate coupled to the status latch makes the self-heal unreachable and lets one transient send error permanently darken a rig baseline kept transmitting through — repaired by keeping send() gated on the bind-set boolean only, with the latch strictly observational.

sonnet/S4: the sACN EADDRNOTAVAIL bind assertion cannot pass because SacnOutput binds with no address — repaired by targeting the setMulticastInterface catch (code EMCASTIFACE) in S6, with a test asserting the diagnostic fires WHILE delivery still succeeds.

sonnet/S4: rewriting the socket lifecycle in a 0-coverage region with only failure-path tests leaves the wire-unchanged claim asserted, not evidenced — repaired by S1's golden packet fixtures byte-compared in S5(b)/S6(a).

fable/S2 and sonnet/S4 (both reviewers): a REQUIRED onStatus lands typecheck-red against four FakeOutput doubles — answered by keeping onStatus optional and calling it as `this.output.onStatus?.(...)`, with test (f) proving a bare PixelOutput still arms.

fable/S2: the BoundUdpSocket collapse omits setBroadcast and no listed verification fails if reuseAddr / setMulticastInterface / setMulticastTTL are dropped in a 0-coverage region — answered by NOT collapsing the socket lifecycle and by adding explicit spy locks on those exact options in S5(e)/S6(e).

fable/S2: 'latching IS the rate limiter' never defines the equality key, so variable dgram message text defeats the dedup — repaired by defining latch equality as (state, code) inside StatusLatch, with a 1000-set test using differing message strings.
fable/S1: exporting generic IPv4 codecs out of the PixLite named barrel misplaces them — repaired by taking the net/ipv4.ts placement instead.

AGENTS.md non-negotiable (raised by the opus reviewer, survived): status emission must not block the render loop — answered by emitting only inside dgram callbacks, never on the send() call path, and locked by S10(a) (100 subscribers, 100 sendFrame calls, zero invocations) and S10(d) (structural no-sync-IO assertion).

Raised by neither reviewer, found while grounding this synthesis: opus's graded universe audit would have reddened the pill for a single-universe-0 sACN config (the all-bad branch) and would have emitted before monitorSettings, breaking the pre-existing 'keeps output monitor destination and source fields filterable' test which asserts events[0] against exactly that fixture (output-manager.test.ts:361-374) — answered by shipping informational-only, emitting after monitorSettings, and pinning the ordering with S9(f).
